title: CMC: Video Transformer Acceleration via CODEC Assisted Matrix Condensing
problem: Video Transformers face significant performance bottlenecks when processing large frame sequences, and existing Vision Transformer accelerators fail to exploit temporal redundancy while incurring substantial overhead from sparse attention prediction modules.
motivation: Video Transformers achieve high accuracy in video understanding tasks but cannot be efficiently deployed to resource-constrained platforms due to prohibitive processing requirements.
method: Video frames are naturally similar across time—a property called temporal redundancy. The approach compresses the matrix data representing this video using a technique called CODEC-assisted matrix condensing, which shrinks the data before the transformer processes it. This reduces both the raw computation needed and the costly overhead from trying to predict which parts of the transformer's attention mechanism actually matter.
key_novelty: The core idea is using CODEC-assisted matrix condensing to exploit temporal redundancy (the similarity between consecutive video frames), which reduces the overhead of predicting which parts of the transformer's attention mechanism matter.
contributions: Identifies that existing ViT accelerators are suboptimal for video transformers due to overlooking temporal redundancy
Proposes CODEC-assisted matrix condensing mechanism for efficient video frame processing
Reduces sparse attention prediction module overhead in accelerator design
Enables practical deployment of video transformers to resource-constrained platforms
primary_theme: video transformer acceleration via CODEC-assisted matrix condensing
